standard.title: Diversity and inclusion
standard.description: describe how valuing diversity influences wellbeing and identify actions that promote inclusion in their communities
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored skills and strategies to develop respectful relationships (AC9HP2P02) and investigated emotional responses (AC9HP2P03). They have practised respectful interaction but have not yet made explicit connections between valuing diversity and wellbeing outcomes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students describe how valuing diversity influences wellbeing and identify actions that promote inclusion in their communities.

nodes.label: Cultural diversity — sharing and celebrating
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise and celebrate the cultural diversity of their class and community.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify and describe at least one cultural practice, game or tradition from their own or a classmate's cultural background.
nodes.typical_width: Explore and share cultural practices, stories and games from multiple cultural backgrounds; reflect on what learning about different cultures adds to the class community.
wider: Explore the diversity of backgrounds, experiences, beliefs and practices of Asian cultures, examining similarities and differences and connecting this to Australian cultural diversity.
Recognise the important role of cultural narratives in First Nations Australian communities — exploring how stories describe diversity and share beliefs and practices.

response_modes.reason: Cultural diversity understanding requires genuine exposure to multiple cultures — not just general awareness that diversity exists. Participation in games, sharing of stories and personal accounts from within the class community grounds the concept in lived experience.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations Australian and Asian cultural contexts are explicitly scoped by the elaborations and represent substantive, meaningful width directions — not supplementary examples but core parts of ACARA's intended cultural scope.
success_criteria: Describes at least one aspect of a cultural background different from their own.
Identifies something they learned from engaging with that cultural perspective.
Explains why cultural diversity is valued in their community.

nodes.label: Diversity, wellbeing and inclusion
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe how valuing diversity influences the wellbeing of individuals and communities.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least one way that valuing diversity benefits the wellbeing of individuals or a community.
nodes.typical_width: Describe multiple connections between valuing diversity and wellbeing, including social, emotional and community dimensions; discuss what happens when diversity is not valued.
wider: Investigate a real community initiative designed to promote inclusion and cultural diversity — examining how it was designed, who it reached, and what wellbeing benefits it aimed to create.
Explore research or statistics on the relationship between inclusion, belonging and mental health in school communities.
nodes.hinge_reason: The causal connection between valuing diversity and wellbeing is the conceptual core of this standard. Students who describe 'being kind' without the wellbeing link cannot meaningfully identify actions that promote inclusion — their proposed actions will lack rationale.

response_modes.reason: Students need to build the explicit causal chain: diversity valued → belonging felt → wellbeing improved. A structured discussion or scenario analysis that makes this chain visible — rather than leaving it implicit — is the key teaching move.

success_criteria: Describes at least one specific connection between valuing diversity and wellbeing.
Explains what 'belonging' means and how it relates to inclusion.
Identifies a consequence for wellbeing when diversity is not valued.

nodes.label: Safe bystander actions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe and practise safe bystander actions when they notice unfair or disrespectful behaviour towards others.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one safe bystander action they could take when they see unfair or disrespectful behaviour.
nodes.typical_width: Describe and practise a range of safe bystander actions across different scenarios (exclusion, disrespect, physical or verbal); evaluate which actions are safe and effective.
wider: Role-play bystander scenarios across different settings (classroom, playground, online) and debrief on the challenges of acting as an upstander and what makes it easier or harder.
Research the concept of 'bystander effect' at an age-appropriate level and discuss how understanding this effect changes their approach to acting when they witness unfair behaviour.

response_modes.reason: Safe bystander action integrates cultural understanding (node 1), wellbeing reasoning (node 2) and strategy selection into a high-stakes social moment. Scenario-based practice with structured reflection is the most effective preparation.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one safe bystander action in a given scenario.
Explains why the action is safe for the bystander as well as the person affected.
Practises the action in a role-play or simulation.
